description: Improve image loading performance and caching — enable Next.js image optimization, add lazy loading to globe markers, add Cache-Control headers, reduce URL batch sizes, add LRU eviction to URL cache

userStories.title: Remove unoptimized prop from gallery Image components
userStories.description: As a user, I want images to be served in modern formats (WebP/AVIF) and responsive sizes so pages load faster, especially on mobile.
acceptanceCriteria: Remove `unoptimized` prop from <Image> in src/presentation/components/gallery/media-grid.tsx
Remove `unoptimized` prop from <Image> in src/presentation/components/gallery/lightbox.tsx (both main image and thumbstrip)
Remove `unoptimized` prop from <Image> in src/presentation/components/albums/album-card.tsx
Remove `unoptimized` prop from <Image> in src/presentation/components/persons/person-card.tsx
Remove `unoptimized` prop from <Image> in src/presentation/components/gallery/face-tags.tsx (both inline and dropdown images)
Remove `unoptimized` prop from <Image> in src/app/(dashboard)/groups/[groupId]/people/[personId]/page.tsx
Verify next.config.ts remotePatterns already allows *.r2.dev and *.r2.cloudflarestorage.com — do NOT change if already correct

Ensure every <Image> has an appropriate `sizes` prop: gallery grid tiles should use responsive sizes like '(max-width: 640px) 50vw, (max-width: 1024px) 33vw, 25vw'; fixed-size avatars use 'sizes="64px"'; lightbox main uses 'sizes="100vw"'
Lightbox main image keeps `priority` prop
npm run type-check passes
npm run build succeeds
userStories.notes: This is the highest-impact change. Next.js image optimizer proxies external images through /_next/image?url=...&w=...&q=75 and auto-negotiates WebP/AVIF. The remotePatterns in next.config.ts already allow *.r2.dev — no config change should be needed. Focus on getting sizes props right for each context: grid columns, lightbox fullscreen, album covers, avatar circles, face tag thumbnails. Do NOT add unoptimized back anywhere. Do NOT change the cluster-popup.tsx <Image> — it already works without unoptimized.

userStories.title: Add loading lazy to globe marker images
userStories.description: As a user, I want globe marker thumbnails to load only when near the viewport so the globe page loads faster.
acceptanceCriteria: In src/presentation/components/globe/create-marker-element.tsx, add loading='lazy' attribute to all elements created for marker thumbnails
Target the thumbnail in single-marker circles and any fan-out cluster thumbnail images
Use img.setAttribute('loading', 'lazy') since these are raw DOM elements (not React JSX)
npm run type-check passes
npm run build succeeds
userStories.notes: These are raw DOM elements created via document.createElement, not React components. Use setAttribute('loading', 'lazy'). This is natively supported in all modern browsers — no polyfill needed. The browser defers the fetch until the image is near the viewport.

userStories.title: Add Cache-Control to geo endpoint
userStories.description: As a developer, I want the /api/media/geo endpoint to return a Cache-Control header so the browser caches the response and avoids redundant round-trips when navigating back to the globe view.
acceptanceCriteria: In src/app/api/media/geo/route.ts, add 'Cache-Control': 'private, max-age=60' header to the successful NextResponse.json() call
Use the same pattern as src/app/api/media/url/route.ts line 61: NextResponse.json(data, { headers: { 'Cache-Control': 'private, max-age=60' } })
Only add header to successful (200) responses, not error responses
npm run type-check passes
npm run build succeeds
userStories.notes: Simple one-liner. The geo endpoint currently returns no Cache-Control header, so every navigation to the globe triggers a fresh DB query. max-age=60 (1 minute) keeps data fresh while preventing rapid re-fetches.

userStories.title: Add LRU eviction to useUrlCache
userStories.description: As a developer, I want the in-memory URL cache to have a maximum size with LRU eviction so it doesn't grow unboundedly for users with thousands of photos.
acceptanceCriteria: In src/presentation/hooks/use-url-cache.ts, add a MAX_CACHE_SIZE constant set to 500
When inserting new entries, if cache.size >= MAX_CACHE_SIZE, evict the least-recently-used entry before inserting
LRU implementation: on cache read (getFromCache), delete and re-insert the key to move it to the end of the Map; on eviction, delete cache.keys().next().value (the oldest entry)
On cache write (when storing fetched URLs), also re-insert to mark as recently used
Existing TTL-based expiration (45 minutes) continues to work alongside LRU — stale entries are still evicted on access
npm run type-check passes
npm run build succeeds
userStories.notes: ES2015 Maps maintain insertion order. Delete-and-reinsert on access moves an entry to 'newest' position. map.keys().next().value gives the oldest key. All O(1) operations. This story must NOT change the public API of useUrlCache — fetchUrls and fetchUrl signatures stay the same. Only internal cache management changes.

userStories.title: Reduce URL batch size to 20 for progressive fetching
userStories.description: As a user, I want the app to fetch thumbnail URLs in smaller batches as I scroll so the initial page load is faster.
acceptanceCriteria: In src/app/(dashboard)/groups/[groupId]/page.tsx, change the thumbnail URL useEffect to fetch in batches of 20 IDs instead of all ready IDs at once
First batch of 20 is fetched immediately on load (covers above-the-fold content)
Remaining IDs are chunked into groups of 20 and fetched sequentially with a small delay or on next animation frame to avoid blocking the main thread
Apply the same batching pattern in src/app/(dashboard)/groups/[groupId]/albums/[albumId]/page.tsx
Apply the same batching pattern in src/app/(dashboard)/groups/[groupId]/people/[personId]/page.tsx
useUrlCache.fetchUrls continues to work unchanged — it already deduplicates cached vs. uncached IDs
No visual regression — images appear progressively as batches resolve, no permanent blank gaps
npm run type-check passes
npm run build succeeds
userStories.notes: The simplest approach: chunk the readyIds array into slices of 20. Fetch the first slice immediately. For remaining slices, use a simple loop with await + requestAnimationFrame or setTimeout(0) between batches. Example: const BATCH_SIZE = 20; const chunks = []; for (let i = 0; i < ids.length; i += BATCH_SIZE) chunks.push(ids.slice(i, i + BATCH_SIZE)); Then fetch chunks[0] immediately, and the rest in sequence. The useUrlCache already deduplicates, so if some IDs are already cached from a previous page visit, those won't be re-fetched.
